resolved_findings.current_summary_quote: For the rest of this encounter, each time that same player must draw a card from the cosmic deck, you may draw it instead, inspect it and give it to them; choose separately for each draw and do not share that information.

primary_source.locator: Mind Flare erratum, cached lines L43–L49 (official FAQ updated May 06, 2009, p1)
primary_source.quote: For the rest of this encounter, each time that player must draw a card from the deck, you may draw it instead, look at it, and then give it to him or her.

resolved_findings.assessment: Separate optional choice for each later cosmic-deck draw by the same player, duration and secrecy match the retained erratum and default-deck FAQ rule.

specific_current_claim_checks.topic: Special destiny designating the offense as defense
specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: If a special card designates you as the defense, the original rulebook also permits trying to drive out a foreign colony in your home system: choose one other player's colony as the defense; all other colonies are unaffected bystanders.
primary_locators: 2008 rulebook p12 Driving Out Foreign Colonies
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: If a player draws his or her own color from the destiny deck (or a special card that designates him or her as the defense), the player may try to eliminate a foreign colony in his or her home system.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: Faithfully retains the printed special-card case, single chosen defending colony and bystander protection.

specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: For random hand-card selection, including compensation, you may see which card backs you select; “at random” means without seeing card faces (FAQ p5).
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: Players are allowed to see which card backs they are selecting.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: Matches the general FAQ definition; no expansion cards are imported.

specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: The ordinary defense-wins-ties rule still applies when totals are equal.
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: The player with the higher total wins, with ties going to the defense.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: The power substitutes lower-total victory without replacing the separate tie rule; this is a faithful application of the common rule.

specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: A successfully made deal is a successful encounter, but is not a win for Cudgel or Barbarian.
primary_locators: 2018 FAQ p3 winning versus successful encounter question
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: A deal does not count as a “win” for effects that do not explicitly mention deals, such as Cudgel, Barbarian, and Guerrilla.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: Accurately applies the later official FAQ and keeps expansion Guerrilla outside the summary.

specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: This explicitly immediate win ends the game when its effect resolves, without waiting for the end of Resolution, unless zapped or specifically interrupted.
primary_locators: Original Masochist JPEG full power and Regroup bar
2018 FAQ p5 ordinary versus immediate victory questions
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: The ordinary end-of-Resolution ruling expressly exempts Masochist; the next FAQ answer says immediate wins end the game unless zapped or specifically interrupted.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: The statement correctly describes the Masochist power’s Regroup win, distinct from the ordinary colony win check.

specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: as an ally during Resolution you may use Void Wild without paying its ship-loss cost, because your protection prevents that sacrifice.
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: Observer must protect all of its ships, whether inside or outside the encounter, when it is an ally; the FAQ expressly permits Void Wild without the losing-ship cost.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: Correctly restricts the permission to the protected role and Resolution timing.

specific_current_claim_checks.topic: Oracle and Sorcerer exchanged card orientations
specific_current_claim_checks.current_summary_quote: The exchange moves the cards without itself flipping either: Sorcerer's original faceup card is now faceup before Oracle, and Oracle's original facedown card is now facedown before Sorcerer until normal Reveal.
specific_current_claim_checks.primary_evidence: The example has Sorcerer play faceup, Oracle select facedown, then Sorcerer switch the selected cards before revealing Oracle’s card.
specific_current_claim_checks.assessment: Supported consequence of the printed sequence: switching changes which card is in front of each player; revealing the originally facedown Oracle card is still subsequent. No additional flip instruction is supplied by either power. Native p14 text was freshly reread and delivered to verify the sequence.

unresolved_sources.status: Honestly documented in summary; not a demonstrated summary error
source_quotes: The chosen alien is placed facedown in front of the player
A player may turn his or her alien sheet faceup at any time in order to use it.
unresolved_sources.rationale: The first is standard setup; the second is specifically an excluded variant. The supplied standard rules do not expressly state the later standard reveal window. The summary accurately records this absence instead of importing the variant rule.
unresolved_sources.completion_limitation: A completely explicit standard setup reveal instruction cannot be established from these supplied sources.

unresolved_sources.status: Honestly documented in summary; not a demonstrated summary error
source_quotes: Yes, any player involved in the encounter may play a reinforcement on either side, regardless of what type of encounter cards were revealed.
Q: Can you play a reinforcement card on a negotiate? A: No.
unresolved_sources.rationale: Both statements occur in the native 2018 FAQ as well as the complete supplied extraction. The supplied sources do not explain the narrower meaning of 'on a negotiate' or resolve a literal contradiction. The summary does not invent a tabletop ruling.
unresolved_sources.completion_limitation: A definitive ruling on this disputed non-attack reinforcement case requires a further publisher clarification.

source_tensions_not_findings.assessment: The printed power explicitly permits equal or higher attacks; the example says higher while discussing attack04 versus attack20. There is no express supplied erratum removing equality. The summary accurately preserves the printed threshold and records the wording difference.
